### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and data only. Nothing here needs software installed at home.

1. Download this week's dataset from the course Drive folder into your `IMSE456` cloud folder.
2. Open the week's Colab notebook and run the first cell to confirm it loads. Ten minutes, from any machine.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you will have at the end

SA7 — the register, the simulation, the criticality table, the Taiga issues, the reconciliation
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Build it yourself — 25 minutes

1. Run the silent pre-mortem. Eight minutes, alone, no talking. The silence is the technique — discussion first destroys it.
2. Convert the stories into a register: risk, probability, impact, RPN, owner, trigger, response type.
3. In Colab, Monte-Carlo the schedule: triangular distributions on the twelve durations, ten thousand trials. Plot the completion-date distribution and compute each activity's criticality index.
4. Build an agent — in Antigravity, or as a Gemini system prompt — that <em>refuses</em> a register entry lacking an owner, a trigger, and a named reference class. Run your own register through it and log every rejection.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now the professional tool — 20 minutes

1. Enter the top eight risks as Taiga issues with severity and assignee.
2. Add contingency to the ProjectLibre schedule as an explicit buffer activity — not as padding hidden inside estimates.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Where do they disagree? — 15 minutes

Your deterministic critical path from Week 6 versus the criticality index from the simulation. Which activities are critical more than forty percent of the time yet never appear on the deterministic path?

Write one paragraph. **This is the graded part** — it is the only thing here a machine cannot check.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Run the check

Run the `verify()` cell at the end of the notebook. It tests your own outputs against tolerances and
prints a completion code. If it fails, you have found your error while it is still cheap to fix —
that is the point of it. Paste the code into your submission.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 65

- [ ] Every row has an owner and an observable trigger
- [ ] the agent rejected at least one entry
- [ ] at least one high-criticality activity is off the deterministic path
:::

::: {.part}

`IMSE456/studio-07/` in your cloud folder. Name files `SA7_yourlastname.*`.

left at home. Submit the PDF and the completion code to Blackboard by the due date above.

**No ProjectLibre?** Do the *Use* half in Smartsheet instead — indented WBS, Gantt, predecessors and critical path all work in a browser. Say so in your submission; it costs you nothing.

## Study loop for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after. It is not graded; it is the fastest way to find out what you have wrong.

```text
Be my tutor on project risk and behavioral bias in estimation. One question
at a time. Make me distinguish cognitive bias from political bias — I keep
collapsing them. Then present the strongest case AGAINST the planning
fallacy account and make me respond to it.
```

See [AI Studio](../ai.qmd) for the Editor and Roommate prompts and the full loop.


::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Label it, verify it, own it.** Append the AI acknowledgement block from the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#how-to-disclose): the tool, the prompt or transcript link, what you changed after reviewing its output, and what it got wrong. Every quantitative result arrives with the check that proves it — **the check is graded, not the output**. "The model said so" is not a defence in this course or in a project review.
:::
